Securities Clarity Act. Operative text amends the securities laws to carve investment contract assets out of the definition of a security, addressed on its face to digital assets raised through blockchain-based protocols. Digital-asset market structure is core category subject matter.

SECURE Notarization Act of 2022 -- the measure named in this category's agenda. Operative text authorises notaries public to perform electronic and remote notarizations for remotely located individuals and compels Federal and State recognition. Remote online notarization is an enumerated category term.

Securities Clarity Act (117th). Operative text excludes investment contract assets from the security definition, expressly for digital assets and blockchain-based protocols. Digital-asset market structure is core category subject matter.

Cryptocurrency Tax Clarity Act. Operative text amends IRC s.6045 to define 'digital asset' as value recorded on a cryptographically secured distributed ledger and to treat digital assets as specified securities for broker reporting. The regulated instrument is the digital asset itself.

Official short title 'Small LENDER Act' and official long title 'Small Lenders Exempt from New Data and Excessive Reporting Act' state the operative effect: exempting smaller lenders from the CFPB small-business-lending data collection under ECOA/Dodd-Frank section 1071. Credit unions are covered financial institutions under that rule, so the measure carries a material credit-union policy nexus. Category is corroborated inside the north-star corpus itself: the same bill family in other Congresses (118:hr:1806, 119:hr:941, same sponsor and same official title) is held in discovery under member_business_lending and cfpb_issues_structural_reform, and discovery routes CFPB section 1071 Regulation B rule disapprovals (118:hjres:50, 118:sjres:32) to member_business_lending. ACU's own advocacy record files section 1071 both as Consumer Protection (letter 1591 on S.557) and as Lending (letter 3441 on the CFPB 1071 rule). The legacy Member Business Lending category is therefore retained and cfpb_issues_structural_reform is added, not substituted. Operative bill text was not reviewed: no BillStatus receipt, GovInfo object or discovery record for this key is held locally and network collection is barred.

Official title is dispositive of subject: congressional disapproval under 5 U.S.C. ch. 8 of a Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection rule under Truth in Lending (Regulation Z) governing use of digital user accounts to access Buy Now, Pay Later loans. Credit unions are Regulation Z creditors, and America's Credit Unions filed its own comment letter on this exact rule (letter 1126, 'Comment Letter to CFPB on BNPL Digital User Accounts', 2024-07-31), which ACU classifies under its Consumer Protection issue area -- establishing the credit-union policy nexus and placing the measure in the outline's Consumer Protection section, not Payment & Technology. The legacy 'Payments' category is unsupported: the north-star Payments boundary is real-time payments, FedNow, instant payment fraud, payment system access, ACH payment, faster payments and payment stablecoin, none of which a Regulation Z consumer-credit rule touches; the legacy retrieval URL shows the measure was pulled in by a legacy Payments query containing a loose 'buy now pay later' term that the outline-derived Payments query does not carry. Discovery's own routing of CFPB rule disapprovals by the rule's subject (Regulation Z credit card penalty fees -> credit_card_consumer_fee_mandates at 118:hjres:121 and 118:sjres:70) and ACU's parallel disapproval letters (396, 1581) fix the corrected categories. Operative text was not reviewed: no BillStatus receipt, GovInfo object or discovery record for this key is held locally.
